neighbours.label: a subject pronoun (He, She, We, I) opening a new sentence or turn after a previous sentence
fire: The teacher looked up from her desk. She smiled and closed the book.
My uncle wiped his hands on a rag. He told us the engine was ruined.
The interview began at noon. We asked about her childhood first.
The phone rang twice before dawn. I let it go to voicemail.
The captain read the letter slowly. He folded it and said nothing.
Rain had soaked the whole camp. We packed up and drove home.
The old woman stopped at the gate. She waved at the children.
The guard pointed at the map. He said the road was closed.
quiet: The teacher looked up from her desk and closed the book with a smile.
My uncle wiped his hands on a rag; the engine, it seemed, was ruined.
The interview began at noon. The first questions were about childhood.
The phone rang twice before dawn. The call went to voicemail.
The captain read the letter slowly. The crew waited in silence.
Rain had soaked the whole camp. The tents were packed up by noon.
The old woman stopped at the gate. The children waved back at her.
The guard pointed at the map. The road, according to him, was closed.

notes: Card: peaks on ' He', 'She', ' We', ' I' starting a sentence after a quote or a full stop. Probe: such pronouns 0.27-0.45; a sentence opening with 'The' ~0.03. Near misses open the next sentence with a noun phrase instead.
